## 1 Introduction {#s-1}

### 1.1 Foreword {#s-1-1}

The European Digital Identity Wallet (EUDIW) is a new concept introduced by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS 2) that enables European citizens, residents and businesses to use a digital identity wallet for identification, authentication, and storage of electronic attestations of attributes. The EUDIW framework introduces novel security, privacy, and interoperability challenges that require clear, well-structured technical requirements.

The Person Identification Data (PID) is the central credential of the EUDIW, acting as the digital identity of its holder. The PID is treated as an object governed by the state model defined in the Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF).

Its lifecycle encompasses multiple stages, from initial issuance through to expiry, revocation or deletion, each presenting distinct security risks and operational requirements. In the present document, "PID" denotes the Logical PID unless a Technical PID is expressly meant; a batch comprises multiple Technical PIDs of the same Logical PID.

This specification addresses the initial issuance, the batch replenishment and the renewal of the PID. It establishes security requirements that the PID Provider must implement to ensure that PID issuance, batch replenishment and renewal processes meet the eIDAS Assurance Level High corresponding to the requirements set out in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.

This specification was developed to define security requirements to cover the risks that can arise during the initial issuance and the renewal of the PID. It is intended to serve as a normative basis for conformity assessment of PID Provider solutions with respect to PID issuance and renewal processes.

The requirements defined in this specification are risk-based and have been derived from an analysis of applicable legislation, reference frameworks, and threat models relevant to the EUDIW ecosystem. A companion risk register documents the risk analysis underpinning the requirements and is maintained as a separate document.

This specification is intended to be used by PID Providers as a normative framework for implementation, and by Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) as a basis for audit and conformity assessment of PID Provider solutions.

### 1.2 Scope {#s-1-2}

This specification defines requirements for the initial issuance and the renewal of the PID within the European Digital Identity Wallet framework. The PID is treated as an object, governed by the state model defined in the Architecture and Reference Framework. The processes covered by this specification meet the requirements for assurance level high as laid down in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502.

This specification covers the following lifecycle events:

- PID Initial Issuance: requirements governing the initial issuance of a PID to a Wallet Unit under sole control of the subject of the PID, from pre-issuance eligibility verification through to the PID being stored and active in the Wallet Unit;

- PID Batch Replenishment: requirements governing the silent, autonomous re-issuance of additional once-only Technical PIDs to a Wallet Unit when the available Technical PIDs fall below a defined threshold or when their attribute values change at the Authentic Source, without user action and without renewed identity proofing of the user;
- PID Renewal: requirements for the re-issuance of a PID when it approaches the end of its validity period. Renewal always requires renewed identity proofing of the user.

The following are explicitly out of scope of this specification:

- PID lifecycle events after issuance (revocation, expiry and deletion), which are covered in a separate specification;
- PID Provider organisational, security and policy requirements;
- PID data model requirements;
- processes at the Authentic Source level;
- requirements regarding the Wallet Unit or Wallet Instance lifecycle;
- Relying Party requirements.

NOTE: This specification does not preclude implementations from imposing additional requirements beyond those specified herein, provided such requirements do not conflict with the provisions of this specification or applicable regulatory requirements.

## 3 Terms & Abbreviations {#s-3}

### 3.1 Terms {#s-3-1}

For the purposes of this specification, the following definitions apply. Terms defined in eIDAS [1] and the Architecture and Reference Framework (ARF) [i.2] are used in accordance with those documents unless otherwise stated.

| Term                                           | Definition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Wallet Instance                                | The software application, including all its components, installed on a Wallet User's device, provided by a Wallet Provider.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Wallet Unit                                    | A unique configuration of a Wallet Solution that includes one or more Wallet Instances, Wallet Secure Cryptographic Applications and Wallet Secure Cryptographic Devices, provided by a Wallet Provider to an individual Wallet User.                                                                                                    |
| Wallet Instance Attestation (WIA)              | An attestation issued by the Wallet Provider certifying that a Wallet Instance is a genuine instance of the Wallet Solution, and carrying the information required to determine its revocation status.                                                                                                                                   |
| Key Attestation (KA)                           | An attestation issued by the Wallet Provider certifying, for one or more public keys, that the corresponding private keys are generated within and are non-extractable from an identified keystore, and describing the storage type and the security certification of that keystore.                                                     |
| Wallet Provider                                | A natural or legal person, or a public body, responsible for providing and operating an EUDIW solution.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Wallet Secure Cryptographic Device (WSCD)      | A hardware or software component that provides a protected execution environment and secure storage for cryptographic keys and operations within the Wallet Unit.                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Wallet Secure Cryptographic Application (WSCA) | The application component that manages cryptographic operations and secure storage within the WSCD.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Person Identification Data (PID)               | A set of data enabling the identity of a natural or legal person to be established, issued by a PID Provider in accordance with eIDAS 2.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Logical PID                                    | The Person Identification Data of a subject as a credential, independent of the individual instances issued to a Wallet Unit. A Logical PID is the type of PID, characterised by its attestation type and its attribute values. A Logical PID does not itself have a validity period or a revocation status; only its Technical PIDs do. |
| Technical PID                                  | An individual issued instance of a Logical PID, stored in a Wallet Unit and presented to Relying Parties, with its own validity period and revocation status. A batch consists of multiple Technical PIDs that represent the same Logical PID, with the same attestation type and attribute values.                                      |
| Administrative Validity Period                 | The period, maintained by the PID Provider for a Logical PID issued to a Wallet Unit, during which the PID Provider may issue further batches of Technical PIDs of that Logical PID to the Wallet Unit without renewed identity proofing of the person.                                                                                  |
| PID Provider                                   | A Member State authority or body, or a private entity designated by a Member State, that issues PID to Wallet Units.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Electronic Attestation of Attributes (EAA)     | A set of data in electronic form that allows attributes about a natural or legal person to be authenticated, issued by a (Qualified) Attestation Provider.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Conformity Assessment Body (CAB)               | A body that performs conformity assessment activities in accordance with applicable standards and legislation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Activation      | The process by which a Wallet Unit is initialised, configured, and bound to a specific Wallet Wallet User, device, and cryptographic key material, rendering it operational.    |
| Suspension      | A temporary, reversible disabling of a Wallet Unit by the Wallet Provider, preventing its use until the suspension is lifted.                                                   |
| Revocation      | A permanent, irreversible invalidation of a Wallet Unit, after which the Wallet Unit cannot be reinstated.                                                                      |
| Migration       | The process of transferring the state of a Wallet Unit from one device to another while maintaining continuity of the Wallet Wallet User's wallet identity and credentials.     |
| Key Material    | Cryptographic keys and associated data generated, stored, and managed within the WSCD for the purpose of securing Wallet Unit operations.                                       |
| Assurance Level | A classification of the degree of confidence in the claimed identity of a person or the integrity of a device, as defined in Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502. |

## 4 Relation to Resilience & High Assurance {#s-4}

### 4.1 Resilience {#s-4-1}

For the purpose of this specification, resilience refers to the ability of the PID issuance and PID lifecycle-management processes to maintain their intended security, integrity and trust properties when exposed to attacks, attempted fraud, compromise, operational failure or misuse. It does not refer to organisational resilience under NIS2 or product-development and vulnerability-handling obligations under the Cyber Resilience Act.

PID issuance and lifecycle management are security-critical processes because they determine whether Person Identification Data is issued to the correct person, bound to an authentic and trustworthy Wallet Unit, maintained on the basis of current and authoritative information, and revoked, expired or otherwise made unusable when the conditions for its continued use no longer apply. The attached specification treats PID as the central credential of the EUDI Wallet and identifies distinct risks throughout initial issuance, batch replenishment and renewal.

These processes are exposed to attackers with a high attack potential. Such attackers may have substantial expertise, resources and time and may combine technical attacks with identity fraud, social engineering, compromised devices, stolen or cloned identity documents, manipulation of issuance requests, interception or modification of communications, compromise of cryptographic keys, exploitation of exceptional lifecycle paths and abuse of legitimate support, recovery or revocation procedures. An attacker may also attempt to conceal the compromise by operating a second Wallet Unit while the rightful citizen's Wallet Unit continues to function normally.

The consequences of a successful attack may extend beyond the compromise of an individual process or technical component. An attacker could obtain a genuine PID in another person's name, bind a PID to cryptographic keys under the attacker's control, continue obtaining Technical PIDs through batch replenishment, renew a PID without the rightful citizen's involvement, prevent or delay effective revocation, or cause the PID Provider to rely on outdated or manipulated identity data. Such a compromise could enable unauthorised use of the citizen's digital identity and could remain undetected if the lifecycle processes are assessed only as separate transactions.

Resilience shall therefore be established through process requirements covering the complete PID lifecycle and the transitions between lifecycle events. These requirements shall ensure, as applicable, that:

- identity proofing and verification resist impersonation, replay, document cloning, relay, injection and manipulation;
- the authenticity, validity and status of identity evidence are established before a PID is issued or renewed;
- the PID is issued only to an authentic and appropriately trusted Wallet Unit;
- issuance, replenishment and renewal requests are fresh, authorised and cryptographically bound to the relevant Wallet Unit and PID;
- PID binding keys are generated and held in an appropriately protected cryptographic environment, and possession of the corresponding private keys is demonstrated;
- PID attributes are obtained from the applicable Authentic Source and remain complete, correct and current;

- batch replenishment cannot be used to bypass renewed identity proofing, prolong a compromised PID relationship or supply an uncontrolled Wallet Unit indefinitely;
- renewal re-establishes the required identity assurance and does not rely solely on the continued possession of an existing Wallet Unit or credential;
- anomalous, repeated or conflicting issuance and lifecycle events are detected, recorded, investigated and responded to;
- the rightful citizen is informed, through an appropriate channel independent of the Wallet Unit, of security-relevant issuance and lifecycle events;
- compromise, loss of control or invalidity results in the appropriate restriction, suspension, revocation, expiry or termination of the affected PID; and
- audit information remains available to support detection, investigation, incident response and conformity assessment.

The attached specification already reflects this process-oriented approach through controls addressing genuine Wallet Instance Attestations, Wallet Trust Evidence, proof of possession, identity-document authenticity, replay protection, authorisation gates, independent citizen notifications, fraud indicators, batch limits, renewed identity proofing and revocation.

No single control is sufficient to ensure resilience. The requirements shall operate as mutually reinforcing safeguards across normal, exceptional and recovery paths. A strong initial identity-proofing process can be undermined by a weak replenishment or renewal process, just as secure PID generation can be undermined by incorrect key binding, insecure delivery, ineffective status management or delayed revocation.

The CAB shall therefore assess not only the design and correct implementation of individual controls, but also whether the PID Provider's processes collectively preserve the intended security properties across the applicable lifecycle events and transitions. This assessment shall consider whether an attacker with high attack potential could circumvent a control by selecting an alternative process path, combining weaknesses across different lifecycle events, or exploiting differences between initial issuance, batch replenishment, renewal and the post-issuance lifecycle processes.

### 4.2 High Assurance {#s-4-2}

The PID Provider is subject to the requirements applicable to assurance level High under Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2015/1502. That Regulation determines assurance levels by reference to the reliability and quality of enrolment, electronic identification means management, authentication, and management and organisation.

Accordingly, the PID issuance and lifecycle-management processes shall meet the requirements applicable to assurance level High and shall preserve the resulting level of assurance throughout the period in which the PID can be issued, replenished, renewed or otherwise used as part of the Wallet User's electronic identification means. Compliance shall not be limited to the initial identity-proofing decision. It shall extend to all process steps that can materially affect the relationship between:

- the identity established by the PID Provider;
- the rightful citizen to whom that identity relates;
- the PID issued in that citizen's name;
- the Wallet Unit to which the PID is issued; and

- the cryptographic keys and authentication mechanisms through which the PID can be used.

For initial issuance, the PID Provider shall establish with the reliability required for assurance level High that the person requesting the PID is the person whose identity is represented by the PID. The PID Provider shall also verify that the receiving Wallet Unit is authentic and sufficiently trustworthy, that the PID is bound to the intended Wallet Unit and dedicated PID binding key, and that delivery takes place only after the required authentication and authorisation steps have been completed. The attached specification gives effect to this through Wallet Unit verification, high-assurance trust evidence, proof of possession, keyprovenance verification, identity proofing, secure authorisation and secure delivery requirements.

The PID issuance and lifecycle-management processes shall, in addition, ensure that the PID is placed and remains under the sole control of the rightful citizen. In the context of this specification, sole control means that the exercise of the PID and the cryptographic capabilities bound to it requires the involvement or authorisation of the correctly identified citizen and cannot be exercised independently by another person, device, Wallet Unit, provider or intermediary.

Sole control shall be established and preserved through a combination of identity, process and technical controls. These controls shall ensure that:

- identity proofing relates to the citizen for whom the PID is generated;
- the issuance decision is bound to the same identity-proofing session and authorised issuance transaction;
- the PID is issued only to the intended Wallet Unit;
- the PID is bound to a dedicated public key for which the intended Wallet Unit has demonstrated possession of the corresponding private key;
- the private key is generated and retained in an appropriately protected cryptographic environment and cannot be exported or independently exercised by the PID Provider;
- authentication of the citizen and the Wallet Unit is successfully completed before the PID is released;
- a PID cannot be issued silently to an additional Wallet Unit without the required detection, confirmation and notification controls;
- replenishment cannot transfer control to another Wallet Unit or continue after reliable evidence that the Wallet Unit is no longer under the citizen's control;
- renewal includes renewed identity proofing at the assurance level required for initial issuance and proof that the request relates to the existing PID and Wallet Unit;
- changes to registered contact methods cannot be used to redirect authorisations and security notifications to an attacker; and
- the rightful citizen has an effective means to recognise and respond to unauthorised issuance or lifecycle events.

The sole-control objective is not satisfied merely because a valid PID has been technically delivered to a Wallet Unit. It requires reasonable assurance that the Wallet Unit and the PID binding keys are controlled by the same rightful citizen whose identity was established during identity proofing. A technically valid issuance to a genuine Wallet Unit would still fail this objective if that Wallet Unit were controlled by an attacker or if the issuance had been induced through impersonation, social engineering, unauthorised contact-method substitution or manipulation of the citizen.

Batch replenishment requires particular safeguards because it issues further Technical PIDs without renewed identity proofing. The attached specification therefore requires replenishment to remain within the Administrative Validity Period and to be cryptographically bound to the Wallet Unit holding the existing Logical PID. It also requires replenishment to stop when reliable information indicates that the Wallet Unit is no longer under the legitimate user's control. These controls are necessary to prevent a compromised Wallet Unit or stolen refresh mechanism from extending an attacker's control by continuously obtaining new Technical PIDs.

Renewal shall not be treated as a mere extension of technical validity. Because renewal establishes a new Administrative Validity Period, the PID Provider shall repeat identity proofing at the assurance level required for initial issuance and shall verify that the renewal request originates from the Wallet Unit holding the Logical PID concerned. The attached specification requires renewed identity verification and proof of possession of the private key corresponding to the existing PID binding public key.

The requirements for assurance level High and sole control are complementary. Assurance level High establishes the required confidence in the citizen's identity and in the processes supporting the electronic identification means; sole control ensures that the capabilities resulting from that identity relationship can be exercised only by the rightful citizen. A failure of sole control can therefore negate the practical value of correctly performed highassurance identity proofing.

The CAB shall assess whether the PID issuance and lifecycle-management processes provide an end-to-end and continuously maintained chain of assurance. The assessment shall verify that assurance level High and sole control are preserved across initial issuance, batch replenishment, renewal and their interfaces with revocation, expiry and deletion. It shall also verify that exceptional, alternative and recovery paths do not permit the identity-proofing, binding, authentication, authorisation, notification or revocation controls of the normal process to be bypassed.

## 5 Lifecycle Event: PID Initial Issuance {#s-5}

Purpose of this chapter: Govern the initial issuance of a PID to a Wallet Unit under sole control of the subject of the PID. Ensure rigorous identity verification, secure cryptographic binding between the PID and the Wallet Unit, and secure delivery of the PID. This covers the full process from pre-issuance eligibility verification through to the PID being stored and active in the Wallet Unit. NOTE: The identity verification and the creation of the PID data are the responsibility of the PID Provider interacting with the Authentic Source. This chapter covers the technical requirements that govern the issuance interaction between the PID Provider and the Wallet Unit.

### 5.1 Pre-Issuance Requirements and Eligibility {#s-5-1}

ISS-5.1-01: The PID Provider shall not issue a PID to a Wallet Unit that already holds an active Logical PID issued by that PID Provider.

## Guidelines

- In practice, the PID Provider checks its own records for an active Logical PID already issued to the same Wallet Unit and does not issue a further one to that unit. This concerns a distinct Logical PID; issuing further Technical PIDs of the same Logical PID (for example during batch replenishment) is a separate operation and is not precluded by this requirement.
- Without this check a single Wallet Unit could accumulate several active Logical PIDs, giving an attacker who controls or clones the unit multiple parallel credentials and complicating later revocation.
- The check is commonly performed against the PID Provider's administration or status service, keyed on the Wallet Unit identifier recorded at issuance.
- A CAB verifies that a second issuance request from a unit already holding an active PID is refused, for instance by reviewing the issuance procedure and status records and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.1-02: The PID Provider shall cancel a PID that has been generated but not issued within the maximum retention period defined in its documented issuance procedures, together with the personal data associated with that PID.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider defines in its documented procedures how long a PID that was created but never delivered is retained, and removes both the PID object and its associated personal data once that period elapses.
- Retaining created-but-undelivered PIDs and their source data indefinitely widens the exposure window for a data breach and leaves orphaned credentials that could later be misused.
- This is typically realised by a scheduled clean-up driven by a timestamp recorded when the PID object is created, with the retention period fixed by a documented risk assessment.
- A CAB reviews the documented retention period and clean-up procedure, inspects retention timestamps, and confirms that expired created-but-unissued PIDs and their data are removed.

ISS-5.1-03: [CONDITIONAL] Where a PID is generated in advance of issuance, the PID Provider shall re-verify, immediately before issuance, that no ground preventing issuance has arisen since the PID was generated, including loss of eligibility, a change in the attributes held by the authoritative population register, decease, a fraud signal, or the identity document having been reported lost or stolen.

## Guidelines

- Where a PID is produced some time ahead of the moment of issuance (for instance when creating PIDs in batches), the PID Provider repeats, immediately before release, the checks that could have changed in the interval, such as eligibility, register attributes, decease, fraud signals, or a lost or stolen document.
- A PID generated in advance can become invalid before it is delivered; without a fresh check an implementation could hand over a credential that no longer reflects the authoritative source or that relates to a compromised document.
- Implementations commonly re-query the authentic population register and the document status source at the point of release and compare the result against the state captured at generation time.
- A CAB verifies that release is blocked when a ground preventing issuance arises between generation and delivery, for instance by reviewing the pre-issuance reverification step and testing a simulated occurrence.

ISS-5.1-04: The PID Provider shall not issue a PID to a Wallet Unit of a Wallet Provider while an active Logical PID issued by that PID Provider in the name of the same person is held in another Wallet Unit of that same Wallet Provider, unless the Technical PIDs of that Logical PID have been revoked in accordance with ISS-5.1-05.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider checks, before issuing, whether the person already has an active Logical PID in a Wallet Unit provided by the same Wallet Provider as the Wallet Unit now requesting a PID. If so, the PID Provider either refuses the issuance or issues only after the older Logical PID has been revoked.
- Without this check, an attacker who installs the wallet application of the same Wallet Provider on a second device and obtains a PID in the victim's name ends up with a working second Wallet Unit next to the victim's own, and nobody notices that the same person now holds two Wallet Units at one Wallet Provider.
- The PID Provider derives the Wallet Provider from the issuer of the Wallet Instance Attestation validated under ISS-5.2-02 and compares it with the Wallet Provider recorded under ISS-5.7-16 for the active Logical PIDs of that person. This requirement sets no maximum on the number Wallet Providers where a person holds a Wallet Unit. A refusal message to the Wallet Unit does not reveal the existence of the other Wallet Unit (see ISS-5.7-19).
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the documented issuance flow and the PID Provider's administration, for instance by inspecting the rule that compares the Wallet Provider of the requesting Wallet Unit with the Wallet Providers recorded for the person's active Logical PIDs, and by examining past issuance records for the absence of two active Logical PIDs of one person at one Wallet Provider.

ISS-5.1-05: The PID Provider shall revoke the Technical PIDs referred to in ISS-5.1-04 only after all other conditions for issuing the further PID have been met, including the confirmation required by ISS-5.4-04 where that requirement applies.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider revokes the older Logical PID of the same Wallet Provider as the last step before issuing the new one, and only once the person has confirmed the new issuance through the registered contact methods.
- If the older Logical PID were revoked as soon as a second Wallet Unit asks for a PID, an attacker could lock the victim out of the victim's own working Wallet Unit by starting an issuance at the same Wallet Provider without ever completing it.
- The PID Provider performs the revocation as part of the same transaction that issues the further PID, so that a failed or abandoned issuance leaves the existing Logical PID untouched. Revocation of the older Technical PIDs is recorded in the status mechanism of the PID Provider, as for other revocations (see REP-6.1-04).
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the issuance flow and its state handling, for instance by examining the point at which revocation of the older Logical PID is triggered and by inspecting records of abandoned issuance attempts that show the older Logical PID remained active.

### 5.2 Wallet Unit Verification {#s-5-2}

ISS-5.2-01: The PID Provider shall verify, before issuing a PID, that the Wallet Unit presents a Wallet Instance Attestation that is valid, has not expired, and has not been revoked.

## Guidelines

- Before issuing, the PID Provider confirms that the Wallet Instance Attestation presented by the unit is currently valid, within its validity period, and not revoked.
- Accepting an expired or revoked Wallet Instance Attestation would let a decommissioned or untrusted wallet obtain a PID.
- Validation typically combines signature verification of the attestation with a freshness and status check against the issuer's revocation information.
- A CAB inspects the verification logic and tests issuance with expired and with revoked attestations to confirm both are rejected.

ISS-5.2-02: The PID Provider shall verify, before issuing a PID, that the issuer of the Wallet Instance Attestation is present in the applicable trusted list.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider confirms that the party that issued the Wallet Instance Attestation appears in the applicable trusted list before relying on the attestation.
- Without this check an attestation minted by an untrusted or rogue provider could be accepted as genuine.
- This is done by resolving the attestation issuer against the current trusted list published for the ecosystem.
- A CAB reviews the trusted-list resolution step and tests that an attestation from an issuer absent from the list is rejected.

ISS-5.2-03: The PID Provider shall not issue a PID unless the Wallet Unit has provided the Wallet Trust Evidence required to establish that its cryptographic device satisfies the conditions for Assurance Level High.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider requires Wallet Trust Evidence demonstrating that the unit's cryptographic device meets the conditions for high assurance before it issues a PID.
- Without evidence of a sufficiently strong device, a PID could be bound into a wallet whose key protection does not meet the required assurance level.
- The Wallet Trust Evidence is typically accompanying the attestation and is evaluated against the high-assurance device criteria.
- A CAB verifies that issuance is refused when the evidence does not establish highassurance device properties, for instance by reviewing the evidence-evaluation step and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.2-04: The PID Provider shall not bind a PID to a public key unless it has verified proof of possession of the corresponding private key as specified in CRED-REQ-PROC-4.6.2.1-0 of [5].

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider binds the PID to a public key only after the unit has proven that it holds the matching private key.
- Binding to a public key without proof of possession would allow a PID to be bound to a key the wallet does not actually control, enabling credential theft.
- A conformant implementation uses the key proof of the Credential Request defined in the referenced issuance profile: the Wallet signs a provider-issued nonce with the private key that the PID will be bound to (the proof-of-possession, or proofs-to-jwt, mechanism), and the PID Provider verifies that signature against the attested public key. A key-attestation-only variant, which carries no such signed proof, does not satisfy this requirement because it does not prove possession.
- A CAB verifies that issuance does not complete when proof of possession is absent or invalid, for instance by testing both scenarios.

ISS-5.2-05: The PID Provider shall verify, using the key provenance attestation provided during issuance, that the PID binding key pair is generated and held in a cryptographic device certified at a level appropriate for Assurance Level High.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider checks, using the key provenance attestation, that the PID binding key pair was generated and is held in a device certified at the level appropriate for high assurance.
- If the binding key were generated or stored outside a suitably certified device, the private key could be extracted or cloned, undermining the security of every later presentation.
- The key provenance attestation supplied during issuance is evaluated against the certification level recorded for the device.
- A CAB reviews the provenance-attestation check and confirms that keys not demonstrably held in an appropriately certified device are rejected.

ISS-5.2-06: The PID Provider shall not rely on trusted-list data whose current validity cannot be confirmed when validating the Wallet Unit.

## Guidelines

- When validating the Wallet Unit the PID Provider uses trusted-list data whose current validity it can confirm, rather than a cached or unverifiable copy.
- Relying on stale trusted-list data could cause the PID Provider to trust an issuer that has since been removed or to miss a revocation.
- Implementations typically refresh the trusted list within a defined freshness window and verify the list's own signature and issue time before use.
- A CAB inspects the trusted-list handling configuration and confirms that outdated or unverifiable list data is not used for validation.

### 5.3 User Identity Verification {#s-5-3}

#### 5.3.1 General Requirements {#s-5-3-1}

ISS-5.3-01: The PID Provider shall verify that the unique identifier established for the subject during identity proofing corresponds to the identity that was authenticated in the same identity-proofing session.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider confirms that the unique identifier it assigns to the subject belongs to the very identity that was authenticated in the same proofing session, so that the identifier and the proofed identity cannot become mismatched.
- If the identifier were taken from a different session or source, a PID could be issued carrying one person's identifier over another person's proofed identity.
- In the Netherlands the unique identifier is the BSN obtained through the polymorphic pseudonym-derivation step of the eID scheme; a conformant implementation derives it within the same authenticated session as the document authentication and ties it to that session's result.
- A CAB verifies that an identifier originating outside the current proofing session is not accepted, for instance by reviewing the session handling and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-02: The PID Provider shall not introduce, into the PID or into the data it generates during issuance, any identifier or reused value - other than the PID attributes themselves - that would enable a third party to correlate separate Technical PIDs or issuance events independently of the attributes disclosed under the User's control from PID representations.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider ensures that, apart from the PID attributes themselves, it places no identifier or reused value in the PID or in the issuance data that a third party could use to link separate Technical PIDs or issuance events.
- Even under selective disclosure, a non-attribute correlation handle left in the credential - such as a reused binding public key, a static credential serial, or reused salts - would let an attacker or colluding relying parties link two separate presentations that each reveal different attributes, establishing that both attributes belong to the same person even though no common identifying attribute was disclosed.
- Implementations avoid embedding document serial numbers, static issuance references, or other stable identifiers in credential data, using per-credential or salted values instead.
- A CAB verifies whether separate issuances for the same person share a correlatable value, for instance by inspecting the issued PID and the issuance data for stable identifiers.

#### 5.3.2 Identity Proofing Using a Digital Identity Document {#s-5-3-2}

The requirements in the present clause apply where the identity proofing of the subject is performed by electronic authentication of a digital identity document, such as the electronic identity function of an identity card or a driving licence recognized as identity document AL High by the member state.

ISS-5.3-03: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall verify, during identity proofing, that the presented identity document chip is genuine and has not been cloned, using the chip's active authentication mechanism or an equivalent anti-cloning mechanism.

## Guidelines

- During identity proofing the PID Provider confirms that the document chip is authentic and not a clone, using the chip's active authentication or an equivalent anti-cloning mechanism.
- A cloned chip would let an attacker replay copied document data to impersonate the legitimate holder.
- This is achieved through the chip's challenge-response active authentication, or a chipauthentication mechanism of equivalent strength, executed live against the chip.
- A CAB verifies that authentication fails against a cloned chip, for instance by testing proofing with a simulated clone.

ISS-5.3-04: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall accept the identity document only if validation of the issuer signature on the chip data against the country signing public key infrastructure returns a complete, fully-passed result.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider accepts the document only when the issuer signature over the chip data validates completely against the country signing infrastructure, with no partial or failed result.
- Accepting a document whose signature only partly validates could admit forged or tampered chip data.
- Validation checks the document security object signature and its certificate chain to the country signing certificate authority, treating any incomplete result as a failure.
- A CAB verifies that documents with invalid or partially validating signatures are refused, for instance by testing both cases.

ISS-5.3-05: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall establish that the identity document chip is read live during the identity-proofing session.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider establishes that the chip is read live during the proofing session rather than from an earlier capture.
- A read that is not live would allow replay of previously captured chip data belonging to another person or session.
- Liveness is established through the interactive chip protocol executed in real time during the session, using session-bound challenges.
- A CAB verifies that the session does not complete when a previously captured chip readout is injected, for instance by testing that scenario.

ISS-5.3-06: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall not accept a previously captured or stored chip readout in place of a live read of the identity document.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider does not accept a stored or previously captured chip readout in place of a live read.
- Permitting stored readouts opens the door to replay attacks using data harvested from an earlier interaction.
- Implementations bind the accepted chip data to freshness values generated for the current session and reject data that lacks them.
- A CAB verifies that stored readout data is rejected, for instance by reviewing the freshness binding and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-07: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document and a status service for that identity document is available, the PID Provider shall check the status of the presented identity document before completing identity proofing.

## Guidelines

- Where a status service exists for the document type, the PID Provider checks the presented document's status before completing proofing.
- Without a status check, a document that has been reported invalid at its source could still be used to obtain a PID.
- The provider queries the available document status service and treats a negative or unavailable status according to its documented policy.
- A CAB verifies that the status check is performed where a service exists and that a document flagged in that service is refused, for instance by testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-08: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall not complete identity proofing where the status check, or any other information available to it, indicates that the identity document is reported lost, stolen, or revoked.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider does not complete identity proofing with a document that is reported lost, stolen, or revoked.
- Proceeding with a reported document would let a person in unlawful possession of it obtain a PID in the rightful holder's name.
- The reported status is obtained from the applicable document status source and, when positive, stops the proofing flow.
- A CAB verifies that proofing does not complete for a document in any reported blocking state, for instance by testing each state.

ISS-5.3-09: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall complete identity proofing only after the chip of the identity document has confirmed successful verification of the document PIN.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider completes proofing only after the chip has confirmed that the document PIN was verified successfully.
- Without confirmed PIN verification, mere possession of the document, without the holder's secret, would suffice to obtain a PID.

- The chip reports successful PIN verification within the authenticated session before proofing is treated as complete.
- A CAB verifies that identity proofing does not complete when the chip has not confirmed PIN verification, for instance by testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-10: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall protect the exchange in which the identity document is electronically authenticated against interception and modification by a party interposed between the identity document and the PID Provider.

## Guidelines

- In practice the PID Provider ensures that the data exchanged while the identity document is electronically authenticated cannot be read or altered by any component that merely carries the traffic between the document and the PID Provider.
- Without this protection, a party interposed between the document and the PID Provider could relay or alter a genuine authentication in real time, obtaining a PID in the legitimate holder's name or binding it to data that the attacker controls.
- Protection is commonly achieved with a channel that is end-to-end encrypted and integrity-protected between the document's secure chip and the PID Provider, so that intermediate components cannot access or modify the cleartext of the exchange.
- A CAB verifies that a party interposed between the document and the PID Provider can neither read nor modify the exchange, for instance by reviewing the channel design and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-11: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall record the number of failed PACE or PINverification attempts that occurred, within the same identity-proofing session, before a successful attempt.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider counts how many PACE or PIN-verification attempts failed within an identity-proofing session before the attempt that succeeded, and keeps that count.
- An attacker guessing or trying a small set of likely PINs against a lost, stolen, or borrowed document may eventually succeed within the chip's own retry limit; without a record of the failed attempts that preceded that success, the PID Provider would have no way to distinguish it from a legitimate user's single mistyped PIN.
- This count is available from the same PACE/PIN-verification exchange the identityproofing session already performs and is written to the session record alongside the successful outcome.
- A CAB verifies that the count of failed PACE or PIN-verification attempts preceding success is recorded, for instance by reviewing session records and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-12: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall flag, for investigation, an identity-proofing session in which the number of failed PACE or PIN-verification attempts before a successful attempt exceeds a defined threshold.

## Guidelines

- When an identity-proofing session shows more failed PACE or PIN-verification attempts before success than a threshold the PID Provider has defined, the PID Provider raises that session for investigation.

- Without such a flag, a successful PIN-guessing attack would result in a PID being issued exactly as if the legitimate holder had authenticated normally, leaving no operational signal that anything unusual occurred.
- The threshold is set by the PID Provider's own fraud-management process, informed by the count kept under ISS-4.3-11.
- A CAB verifies that a failed-attempt count exceeding the defined threshold results in the session being flagged, for instance by reviewing the threshold configuration and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-13: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall record the identity document's chip identifier together with the national identification number established during each identity-proofing session.

## Guidelines

- Each time the PID Provider completes identity proofing, it records the presented document's chip identifier alongside the national identification number the session established.
- A cloned or shared document chip could otherwise be presented across multiple identity-proofing sessions, each establishing a different national identification number, without the PID Provider ever recording the fact that the same chip identifier was involved each time.
- This pairs the chip identifier already read during identity proofing with the resulting national identification number in the PID Provider's administration.
- A CAB verifies that chip identifier and national identification number are recorded together for each identity-proofing session, for instance by reviewing the administration data and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.3-14: [CONDITIONAL] If the PID Provider performs the identity proofing based on a digital identity document, the PID Provider shall flag, for investigation, an identity document chip identifier that has been recorded together with more than one distinct national identification number.

## Guidelines

- When the PID Provider's records show the same document chip identifier paired with more than one distinct national identification number, it raises that chip identifier for investigation.
- A cloned document, a shared document, or a compromised derivation step could each let one physical chip be used to obtain PIDs for more than one claimed identity; without cross-referencing across sessions, none of these would come to light.
- This check runs against the pairing already recorded under ISS-4.3-13 and can be performed at the time of each new identity-proofing session or on a periodic basis.
- A CAB verifies that a chip identifier recorded against more than one national identification number results in a flag, for instance by reviewing the cross-referencing mechanism and testing the scenario.

### 5.4 PID Issuance Request and Authorisation {#s-5-4}

ISS-5.4-01: The PID Provider shall reject an issuance request that does not contain a valid, unused freshness value bound to the authenticated wallet session.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider rejects any issuance request that lacks a valid, single-use freshness value tied to the authenticated wallet session.
- Without a bound single-use freshness value, a captured issuance request could be replayed to obtain an unauthorised PID.
- A server-generated nonce or equivalent, bound to the session and consumed on first use, accompanies each request.
- A CAB verifies that a replayed request, and a request with a missing or reused freshness value, are both rejected, for instance by testing both cases.

ISS-5.4-02: The PID Provider shall not authorise issuance unless every required precondition has been successfully completed, comprising Wallet Unit trust verification, user identity verification, and the eligibility check.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider authorises issuance only when every prerequisite, namely unit trust verification, identity verification, the eligibility check, has been completed successfully.
- Authorising issuance with a skipped prerequisite could produce a PID that was never properly verified or consented to.
- A single authorisation gate checks the recorded outcome of each prerequisite step before issuance proceeds.
- A CAB verifies that issuance is blocked when any one prerequisite is incomplete, for instance by reviewing the authorisation gate and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.4-03: The PID Provider shall log an issuance request rejected for failing a freshness or replay check, together with the reason for rejection.

## Guidelines

- Each time the PID Provider rejects an issuance request because it fails a freshness or replay check, it records that rejection and the reason in a log.
- Without this record, repeated replay attempts against the same Wallet Unit or credential would be invisible even though each individual attempt is correctly blocked, so a sustained attack would not be noticed until an issuance eventually succeeded through some other weakness.
- The rejection log entry is typically written by the same component that performs the freshness or replay check, capturing the check that failed and the request context.
- A CAB verifies that rejected replay or freshness-check failures are logged with their reason, for instance by reviewing log samples and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.4-04: [CONDITIONAL] Where one or more contact methods are registered for a person, the PID Provider shall not authorise the issuance of a PID in that person's name to a Wallet Unit that does not yet hold a Logical PID of that person unless the person has entered in the issuance flow the one-time code that the PID Provider has sent through a registered contact method.

## Guidelines

- Issuance of a PID to a new Wallet Unit is confirmed with a one-time code that reaches the person through at least one of the contact methods registered earlier, so that the person actually decides whether a new Wallet Unit is set up in their name.

- An attacker who passes identity proofing with stolen or relayed credentials and installs a wallet on a device of the attacker's own gets a working PID in the victim's name, and the victim finds out only afterwards. Because the code goes only to the contact methods of the person, the attacker cannot complete the issuance without the cooperation of the person.
- The code is sent by text message to the registered mobile number or by e-mail to the registered address, and the person types it into the issuance flow. Registration and verification of contact methods is covered by ISS-5.7-20 and ISS-5.7-21. A person who no longer has access to a registered contact method first replaces it as described in ISS-5.7-24. This requirement does not apply to renewal or replenishment of a Logical PID that is already held by the Wallet Unit.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the issuance flow and the authorisation logic, for instance by examining that issuance to a new Wallet Unit is not authorised without a matching code from a registered contact method, and by inspecting records of past issuances for the presence of the code confirmation.

ISS-5.4-05: The PID Provider shall ensure that every message that carries a one-time code under ISS-5.4-04 names the Wallet Provider of the Wallet Unit concerned, states that a new Wallet Unit is being set up in the person's name, warns the person never to share the code with anyone, and contains no link, QR code, or telephone number to call.

## Guidelines

- The message that delivers the code tells the person which Wallet Provider the request comes from, that a new Wallet Unit is being set up, and that the code is never to be shared with anyone.
- A fraudster who has persuaded a victim to forward a code, for example by posing as a bank employee or as the government, depends on the victim not understanding what the code is for. A message that states what is about to happen, and that contains nothing to click or call, gives the victim the information to recognise the attempt and removes the fraudster's route to redirect the victim.
- The message is short and states the three facts in plain language, for instance the name of the Wallet Provider, the words that a new Wallet Unit is being set up in the person's name, and a sentence that if the code is asked for by another person, that the conversation with that person should be halted immediately as this is a very strong sign of fraud. The wording follows the communication charter that applies to the PID Provider and all Wallet Providers.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the templates of the messages and the configuration that fills them, for instance by inspecting a sample of messages sent in the past, and by confirming that each contains the three required statements and no link, QR code or telephone number.

ISS-5.4-06: The PID Provider shall invalidate a one-time code issued under ISS-5.4-04 or ISS-5.7-21 after its first successful use, after the end of a defined validity period, and after a defined number of failed entry attempts.

## Guidelines

- A one-time code works once, for a short time, and for a limited number of attempts.
- A code that stays valid after use, for a long time or for unlimited attempts is exposed to guessing, to reuse after the person has been talked into reading it out, and to replay against a later issuance.
- The PID Provider determines the validity period and the number of attempts as part of its risk assessment, and generates codes with sufficient entropy for the chosen limits.

- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the design and configuration of the code service, for instance by inspecting the validity period and attempt limit that are set, and by examining records of issued codes that show invalidation after use, expiry or failed attempts.

### 5.5 PID Generation and Signing {#s-5-5}

ISS-5.5-01: The PID Provider shall not generate a PID unless a complete and current set of the required attributes has been obtained from the authoritative population register.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider generates a PID only once it holds a complete and current set of the required attributes obtained from the authoritative population register.
- Generating a PID from incomplete or outdated attribute data would issue a credential that misstates the person's authoritative identity.
- The provider retrieves the attributes from the authoritative register at issuance time and confirms completeness before generation.
- A CAB verifies that generation does not proceed with an incomplete attribute set, for instance by reviewing the register-retrieval step and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.5-02: The PID Provider shall populate each mandatory PID attribute in accordance with the applicable national value convention, including the defined fall-back values where an attribute value is not available.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider fills each mandatory PID attribute following the applicable national value convention, using the defined fall-back values where a value is unavailable.
- Inconsistent attribute population or ad-hoc handling of missing values would produce PIDs that relying parties cannot interpret reliably.
- A documented mapping from register fields to PID attributes, including the national fall-back values, drives population.
- A CAB reviews the attribute-mapping documentation and inspects issued PIDs for conformant values and fall-backs.

ISS-5.5-03: The PID Provider shall not fetch, process, or store any optional attribute that has been excluded at national level.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider does not fetch, process, or store any optional attribute that has been excluded at national level.
- Handling excluded attributes would collect or expose personal data beyond what is proportional.
- The set of permitted attributes is configured from national policy, and retrieval or storage of anything outside it is suppressed.
- A CAB verifies that excluded attributes are neither retrieved nor retained, for instance by reviewing the configured attribute set and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.5-04: The PID Provider shall bind the PID to the dedicated PID binding public key provided for that PID and to no other key.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider binds the PID to the dedicated PID binding public key provided for that PID and to no other key.

- Binding to the wrong key, for instance a reused or unrelated key, would let a party other than the intended holder use the credential.
- The provider takes the binding public key from the proof-of-possession step of the same issuance and embeds only that key. The binding public key is the dedicated PID binding key whose generation and protection in the Wallet Unit's certified cryptographic device has been attested to the PID Provider, so that the PID is placed under the sole control of the User and bound to that Wallet Unit alone.
- A CAB verifies that a PID is not bound to any key other than the one presented for that issuance, for instance by inspecting the binding in issued PIDs and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.5-05: The PID Provider shall sign the PID using a signing key whose certificate chains to a trust anchor published in the applicable trusted list.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider signs the PID with a signing key whose certificate chains to a trust anchor published in the applicable trusted list.
- A signing key that is not anchored in the trusted list would produce PIDs that relying parties cannot validate as authentic.
- The signing certificate is issued under a chain terminating at a published trust anchor, and that chain is kept current.
- A CAB verifies the signing certificate chain against the trusted list and inspects a signed PID.

ISS-5.5-06: The PID Provider shall use the PID signing key only within the authorised issuance process.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider uses the PID signing key solely within the authorised issuance process and for no other purpose.
- Use of the signing key outside the controlled issuance process could produce unauthorised or forged PIDs.
- The signing key is held in a protected signing service whose invocation is restricted to the issuance workflow.
- A CAB reviews the access controls and usage logs for the signing key and confirms that its use is confined to PID issuance.

ISS-5.5-07: The PID Provider shall set the validity period of the PID so that it does not exceed the maximum PID lifetime defined by national policy.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider sets the PID validity period so that it does not exceed the maximum PID lifetime defined by national policy.
- An over-long validity period would keep a credential usable well beyond the point where its data or binding can be relied upon.
- The configured maximum lifetime from national policy caps the validity end date computed at generation.
- A CAB reviews the configured maximum and inspects issued PIDs for conformant validity periods.

ISS-5.5-08: The PID Provider shall set the validity period of the PID so that it does not extend beyond the validity of the Wallet Unit to which the PID is issued.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider sets the PID validity so that it does not extend beyond the validity of the Wallet Unit to which the PID is issued.
- A PID outliving its Wallet Unit could remain nominally valid in a unit that is no longer trusted.
- The validity end date is capped at the earlier of the national maximum and the Wallet Unit's own validity.
- A CAB inspects issued PIDs against the corresponding unit validity and confirms that the PID does not outlast the unit.

### 5.6 Secure PID Delivery {#s-5-6}

ISS-5.6-01: The PID Provider shall not release a PID to the Wallet Unit before authentication of the Wallet Unit and of the holder has completed successfully.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider releases the PID to the unit only after both the Wallet Unit and the holder have been authenticated successfully.
- Releasing before authentication completes could deliver a PID to an unverified unit or to someone other than the holder.
- A release gate withholds the PID until both authentication results are confirmed within the session.
- A CAB verifies that no PID is released when either authentication is incomplete, for instance by testing the scenario.

ISS-5.6-02: The PID Provider shall deliver the PID to the Wallet Unit using the issuance protocol specified in [5].

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider delivers the PID over the issuance protocol defined in the referenced normative specification rather than over an ad-hoc channel.
- An unspecified delivery mechanism would lead to interoperability in the EUDIW ecosystem and could omit the mutual authentication and secure-channel properties that the standard issuance protocol guarantees, exposing the PID in transit.
- The delivery uses the issuance protocol profile named in the requirement, including its authentication and secure-transport provisions.
- A CAB verifies an issuance exchange for conformance with the referenced specification, for instance by reviewing the implemented protocol and testing the exchange.

ISS-5.6-03: The PID Provider shall record the outcome of each issuance, including any refusal of the issued PID by the Wallet Unit and any case where the Wallet Unit does not respond.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider records the outcome of each issuance, including any case where the unit refuses the issued PID or when the Wallet Unit does not respond anymore.
- Without recorded outcomes, refusals and failures would go untracked, hindering incident investigation and reconciliation.
- The outcome, including a refusal, is written to the issuance record as the exchange concludes.

- A CAB reviews issuance records and confirms that both successful and refused outcomes are captured.

ISS-5.6-04: The PID Provider shall classify a PID that has left its systems as issued, regardless of whether the Wallet Unit confirms its acceptance.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider treats any PID that has left its systems as issued, even if the unit has not confirmed acceptance.
- If a delivered PID were treated as never issued because acceptance was not confirmed, a credential that actually reached a unit could remain unaccounted for, for example when an acceptance message is lost.
- The provider marks the PID as issued at the point it leaves the provider boundary, independently of any later acceptance confirmation.
- A CAB verifies that a PID which has left the provider is recorded as issued when acceptance confirmation is withheld, for instance by reviewing the state model and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.6-05: The PID Provider shall revoke a PID that it has classified as issued where the Wallet Unit reports that the PID was not accepted.

## Guidelines

- Where the unit reports that a PID it has classified as issued was not accepted, the PID Provider revokes that PID rather than cancelling it.
- Cancelling instead of revoking a PID that may in fact have reached a unit could leave a usable credential outside the revocation status, because a not-accepted report can be a false negative.
- On a not-accepted report for an issued PID, the provider drives it through the revocation path so that its status is published.
- A CAB verifies that a not-accepted report for an issued PID results in the PID being revoked and not cancelled, for instance by testing the scenario.

### 5.7 Post-Issuance Status Service Registration {#s-5-7}

ISS-5.7-01: The PID Provider shall register each issued PID, including its identifier, its validity end date, and its status, in the PID Provider's administration and status service.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider records each issued PID, with its identifier, validity period, and status, in its administration and status service.
- An unregistered PID could not be tracked or revoked, and its status could not be published to relying parties.
- Registration writes the identifier, validity, and status to the status service as part of completing issuance.
- A CAB reviews the status service contents and confirms that issued PIDs appear with the required fields.

ISS-5.7-02: The PID Provider shall record, for each issued PID, the Wallet Unit to which that PID was issued.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider records, for each issued PID, which Wallet Unit it was issued to.

- Without this record the provider could neither prevent a second valid PID from going to the same unit nor detect that an additional wallet has been activated for the same person.
- The Wallet Unit identifier is stored alongside the PID record at issuance and used in later duplicate checks.
- A CAB inspects issuance records and confirms that the issuing-target Wallet Unit is captured for each PID.

ISS-5.7-03: The PID Provider shall record the withdrawal of a PID that has already been delivered to a Wallet Unit as a revocation with a corresponding entry in the status service.

## Guidelines

- When a PID that has already been delivered is withdrawn, the PID Provider records the withdrawal as a revocation with a matching status-service entry.
- Recording a delivered PID's withdrawal as anything other than a revocation would leave relying parties unaware that the credential is no longer valid.
- The withdrawal of a delivered PID is routed to the revocation path, producing a published status change.
- A CAB verifies that withdrawal of a delivered PID produces a revocation entry in the status service, for instance by testing the scenario.

ISS-5.7-04: The PID Provider shall record each issuance event in a tamper-evident log with sufficient detail to support conformity assessment and incident investigation.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider records each issuance event in a log that is protected against tampering and detailed enough for conformity assessment and incident investigation.
- A log that could be altered, or that lacks detail, would undermine after-the-fact investigation and audit.
- Log entries are written to append-only or integrity-protected storage capturing the salient issuance facts and timestamps.
- A CAB reviews the log's integrity protection and confirms that entries carry sufficient investigative detail.

ISS-5.7-05: The PID Provider shall notify the person identified in the PID, through a channel independent of the Wallet Unit, when a PID is issued in that person's name.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider notifies the identified person, over a channel that does not depend on the Wallet Unit, whenever a PID is issued in that person's name.
- Without an independent notification, a PID issued fraudulently in someone's name could go unnoticed by the victim.
- The notification is sent over a channel the person holds independently of the wallet, such as an official government message box or a registered contact method.
- A CAB reviews the notification mechanism and confirms that an out-of-band notice is generated on issuance.

ISS-5.7-05A: The PID Provider shall notify the person in whose name a PID was requested, through a channel independent of the Wallet Unit, when a request to issue a PID in that person's name does not result in issuance because identity proofing or another eligibility check failed, inviting that person to raise an alarm if they did not make the request.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider sends an out-of-band notice not only when a PID is issued (ISS-4.705) but also when an attempt to obtain a PID in a person's name is made and does

not complete, for example because identity proofing failed, asking the person to report the attempt if they did not make it.

- Without notice of a failed attempt, a fraudulent attempt that is stopped by proofing leaves no signal to the targeted person, so an attacker can retry or refine the attempt while the victim remains unaware that their identity is being targeted.
- The notice is sent over the same independent channel used for ISS-4.7-05, addressed to the person named in the request as held by the Authentic Source, and tells the person to raise an alarm if they did not initiate the request; the PID Provider applies rate and content safeguards so the notice itself cannot be used to probe or harass a person.
- A CAB verifies that a failed or refused issuance attempt generates an out-of-band notice to the named person with instructions to report an unrecognised attempt, for instance by testing a request that fails identity proofing.

ISS-5.7-06: The PID Provider shall notify the identified person, through a channel independent of the Wallet Unit, when more than one Logical PID issued by that PID Provider is active in that person's name.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider notifies the person, over a wallet-independent channel, when more than one PID that it has issued is active (has an ongoing valid Administrative Validity Period) in that person's name.
- Several active PIDs for one person can signal that a second wallet has been activated fraudulently, and a person left unaware cannot intervene.
- The provider detects the condition from its own active-PID records per person and triggers the notification.
- A CAB verifies that a notification is generated for the multiple-active-PID condition, for instance by testing the scenario.

ISS-5.7-07: The PID Provider shall offer the person the opportunity to register one or more contact methods that are capable of delivering a notification to the person without delay.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider gives the person the opportunity to register one or more contact methods able to reach them without delay.
- If notifications only reach a channel the person checks infrequently, an attacker's window to misuse a fraudulent PID before the person reacts is much longer.
- The provider offers registration of instantaneous channels, such as a mobile number for text messaging or an email address, in addition to any default channel.
- A CAB reviews the enrolment options and confirms that the person can register an instantaneous contact method.

ISS-5.7-08: The PID Provider shall ensure that the notification referred to in ISS-5.7-06 states explicitly that the activation of a further Wallet Unit that the person did not perform or authorise or that was done on request of someone else, may result in financial loss or identity theft to that person.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider makes the notification about a further active wallet state plainly that an activation the person did not perform or authorise or that was done on request of someone else (potentially an attacker), can lead to financial loss or identity theft.
- A notice that does not convey the concrete consequences may be ignored or the attacker could easily convince the victim that the message can be safely disregarded, so the person fails to act on a genuine fraud signal. In the case of social engineering

the victim is under influence of the attacker and the message should be strong enough to make the victim realize he might be under attack and reconsider whether to continue to follow the instructions of the attacker.

- The notification text names the potential harms in clear, plain language accessible to the recipient.
- A CAB inspects the notification content and confirms that the explicit harm statement is present.

ISS-5.7-09: The PID Provider shall include, in the notification referred to in ISS-5.7-06, a means for the person to revoke the newly issued PID through a low-threshold procedure.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider includes in that notification an easy, low-threshold way for the person to revoke the newly issued PID.
- If revoking a suspicious new PID were difficult, a person who recognises fraud might be unable to stop it quickly enough.
- The notification carries a direct, simple action, such as a single link or short procedure, that revokes the newly issued PID.
- A CAB reviews the notification and confirms that it provides a low-threshold revocation path for the newly issued PID.

ISS-5.7-10: The PID Provider shall require the use of its standard revocation procedure to revoke any PID, other than the newly issued PID referred to in ISS-5.7-09, that is active in that person's name.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider confines the low-threshold revocation offered in the notification to the newly issued PID, and requires any other PID active in the person's name to be revoked through the standard revocation procedure.
- If the low-threshold path could revoke the person's earlier legitimate PID, an attacker could use the notification itself to trick the victim into revoking their genuine credential and locking themselves out.
- The low-threshold action is scoped to the single new PID, while revocation of any preexisting PID is directed to the normal, more deliberate revocation channel.
- A CAB verifies that the notification's low-threshold action cannot revoke a PID other than the newly issued one, and that any other PID requires the standard procedure, for instance by testing the scenario.

ISS-5.7-11: The PID Provider shall record, for each national identification number, the number of Wallet Units to which a PID for that national identification number is currently issued and within its Administrative Validity Period, and the timestamps of each issuance and renewal request relating to that national identification number.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider keeps a running count of active Logical PIDs and a timestamped history of issuance and renewal requests, indexed by national identification number.
- Without such a record, a Logical PID issued into an additional Wallet Unit under someone else's control, alongside the legitimate holder's own working Wallet Unit, would leave no trace an investigator could later use to notice that more than one active PID exists for the same person.
- This is typically implemented as an addition to the PID Provider's existing administration and status service, keyed by national identification number rather than by Logical PID identifier alone; the same record is drawn on for renewal requests under Chapter 6.

- A CAB verifies that the administration records active-Logical-PID counts and request timestamps per national identification number, for instance by inspecting the administration data model and issuing a test PID.

ISS-5.7-12: The PID Provider shall flag, for investigation, a national identification number whose active-Logical-PID count or issuance-or-renewal-request rate exceeds a defined threshold.

## Guidelines

- When the count of active Logical PIDs, or the rate of issuance or renewal requests, for a given national identification number exceeds a threshold the PID Provider has defined, the PID Provider raises that identification number for investigation.
- An attacker who has obtained a genuine PID into an additional Wallet Unit relies on this pattern going unnoticed; without a threshold-based flag, the resulting anomaly in active-PID count would never be surfaced to anyone able to act on it.
- The threshold and the resulting investigative workflow are defined by the PID Provider's own fraud-management process; this requirement only constrains that some such threshold and flagging mechanism exists.
- A CAB verifies that exceeding the defined threshold results in the identification number being flagged, for instance by reviewing the threshold configuration and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.7-13: The PID Provider shall record, where available to it, the network origin or locality indicator of each issuance or renewal request.

## Guidelines
