- Where the PID Provider has access to a network origin or locality indicator for an issuance or renewal request, such as the requesting network's approximate location, it records that indicator with the request.
- Without any locality indicator on record, two issuance or renewal events for the same person occurring in quick succession from geographically implausible locations would look identical to two ordinary, unrelated requests.
- This depends on whatever network-origin information is already available to the PID Provider's issuance and renewal channel; it does not require introducing new means of locating the User.
- A CAB verifies that available network origin or locality indicators are recorded with issuance and renewal requests, for instance by reviewing request records and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.7-14: The PID Provider shall flag, for investigation, two issuance or renewal requests relating to the same national identification number whose recorded network origin or locality indicators are inconsistent with the time elapsed between them.

## Guidelines

- When two issuance or renewal requests for the same national identification number carry locality indicators that could not both be genuine given the time between the requests, for example locations a person could not plausibly travel between in that time, the PID Provider raises that pair of requests for investigation.
- This pattern is a recognised indicator that one of the two requests originates from a party other than the legitimate holder, for example an attacker operating a duplicate Wallet Unit or impersonating the holder from elsewhere, while the holder's own genuine request continues undisturbed.

- The plausibility check compares the recorded locality indicators and elapsed time against a configured travel-speed assumption; it is only meaningful where locality indicators were captured under ISS-4.7-13.
- A CAB verifies that a geographically implausible pair of requests results in a flag, for instance by reviewing the plausibility-check configuration and testing the scenario.

ISS-5.7-15: The PID Provider shall subject each case that this specification requires to be flagged for investigation to a defined investigation and response procedure.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider handles every case that this specification requires to be flagged for investigation through a defined procedure that determines the response, rather than recording the flag and leaving it without follow-up.
- Flagging a suspected fraud or anomaly without a defined follow-up would leave the detection signal unacted upon, so the control would not reduce the risk it was introduced to address.
- The PID Provider maintains an investigation and response procedure, aligned with a recognised fraud-management framework such as ISO 37003 [i.4], that assigns each flagged case for assessment and defines the possible responses.
- A CAB verifies that flagged cases are routed to a defined investigation and response procedure, for instance by reviewing the procedure and tracing a flagged case through it.

ISS-5.7-16: The PID Provider shall record, for each issued PID, the Wallet Provider that provided the Wallet Unit to which the PID was issued and the date of issuance.

## Guidelines

- For every PID, the PID Provider keeps the name of the Wallet Provider of the receiving Wallet Unit and the date on which the PID was issued, in addition to the Wallet Unit recorded under ISS-5.7-02.
- Without these two data, the PID Provider cannot tell a person which Wallet Units are active in their name, cannot recognise a second Wallet Unit at the same Wallet Provider, and cannot route a revocation request or a report to the Wallet Provider concerned.
- The PID Provider takes the Wallet Provider from the Wallet Instance Attestation validated under ISS-5.2-01 and the date from the issuance event logged under ISS5.7-04.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the data model of the administration and by examining a sample of PID records for the presence of the Wallet Provider and the issuance date.

ISS-5.7-17: The PID Provider shall state, in each notification referred to in ISS-5.7-05 and ISS-5.7-06, the Wallet Provider and the date of issuance recorded under ISS-5.7-16 for the Wallet Unit concerned.

## Guidelines

- Each notification names the Wallet Provider and the date, so the person can tell a Wallet Unit they know from one they do not.
- A notification that only says that a PID has been issued does not allow the person to tell their own new device from an attacker's device, and is easily dismissed as routine.
- The Wallet Provider and date are included in the notification text, for instance in the first sentence.

- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the notification templates and by examining a sample of sent notifications for the presence of the Wallet Provider and the date.

ISS-5.7-18: The PID Provider shall list, in the notification referred to in ISS-5.7-06, every Wallet Unit in which an active Logical PID is held in the person's name, stating for each the Wallet Provider and the date of issuance, and invite the person to revoke any Wallet Unit that is suspicious or no longer in use through the standard revocation procedure referred to in ISS-5.7-10.

## Guidelines

- The notification about a further Logical PID gives the person the complete picture: every active Wallet Unit with its Wallet Provider and issuance date, and an invitation to revoke those that are unknown or unused.
- If the person is told only about the newest Wallet Unit, an older fraudulent Wallet Unit, or one that was forgotten after a change of phone, stays active and unnoticed.
- The list is built from the data recorded under ISS-5.7-16. The invitation points to the revocation route to which the person authenticates, and does not offer a revocation link that works from a Wallet Unit.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the notification templates and the logic that builds the list, and by examining a sample of notifications sent where more than one Logical PID was active.

ISS-5.7-19: The PID Provider shall not disclose to a Wallet Unit, or offer through a Wallet Unit a means to revoke, any other Wallet Unit in which a PID is held in the name of the same person.

## Guidelines

- Information about, and revocation of, a person's Wallet Units is available to the person through channels that do not depend on a Wallet Unit, and never through a Wallet Unit itself.
- An attacker who has activated a Wallet Unit in the victim's name could otherwise see the victim's other Wallet Units and revoke them, which locks the victim out and leaves the attacker as sole holder.
- The PID Provider limits the issuance protocol responses to the Wallet Unit to what that Wallet Unit needs, and offers the overview and revocation of Wallet Units only through a route that is not a Wallet Unit, as described in the PID Lifecycle Events Specification [7].
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the interface descriptions of the issuance protocol and by inspecting the responses sent to a Wallet Unit, for instance to confirm that they contain no data about other Wallet Units of the person.

ISS-5.7-20: The PID Provider shall, at the first issuance of a PID in a person's name, collect from the person both a mobile telephone number that is able to receive text messages and an e-mail address, and register them as contact methods under ISS-5.7-07 unless the person explicitly declines.

## Guidelines

- At the first issuance, the person is asked for both a mobile number and an e-mail address, and both are registered unless the person declines.
- If no contact method is registered, the notifications and codes of the PID Provider can only reach a channel that the person checks rarely, and an attacker has a long window to use a fraudulent PID. Two independent channels reduce the risk that a single compromised channel hides the attack.

- The collection is part of the first-issuance flow, after identity proofing. Declining is recorded, so the PID Provider notifies through the channel of ISS-5.7-05 only. A person who declined is offered registration again at each later issuance.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the first-issuance flow and by examining the records of a sample of first issuances for the registered contact methods or the recorded refusal.

ISS-5.7-21: The PID Provider shall register a contact method only after the person has entered a one-time code that the PID Provider has sent to that contact method.

## Guidelines

- A contact method is registered only after the person has shown that they have access to it by entering a code sent to it.
- An attacker who is allowed to register a contact method without proof of access can register a number or address of their own, so that every later warning and code reaches the attacker instead of the victim.
- The code follows ISS-5.4-06. The PID Provider repeats the verification whenever a contact method is added or replaced.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the registration flow and by examining records of registered contact methods for the verification event.

ISS-5.7-22: The PID Provider shall replace a registered contact method only after the person has entered a one-time code that the PID Provider has sent to the contact method that is being replaced, except where ISS-5.7-24 applies.

## Guidelines

- A contact method is changed only with proof of access to the existing one.
- An attacker who has obtained a PID could otherwise replace the contact methods of the victim with their own, so that further warnings and codes no longer reach the victim.
- The code follows ISS-5.4-06 and the new contact method is verified under ISS-5.721. A person who has no access to the contact method being replaced follows ISS5.7-24.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the contact-change flow and by examining records of past changes for the code confirmation.

ISS-5.7-23: The PID Provider shall notify every contact method registered before a change, through that contact method, when a registered contact method has been replaced.

## Guidelines

- Whenever a contact method is replaced, the previous contact methods are told.
- Even a verified change is sometimes the result of social engineering; a notice to the previous contact gives the person the opportunity to see the change and to react.
- The notice states the date of the change and that the change was made. It does not contain the new contact details in full, so that it is useless to a person who intercepts it.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the contact-change flow and by examining a sample of changes for the notification to the previous contact methods.

ISS-5.7-24: The PID Provider shall, where the person has no access to a contact method that is to be replaced, replace it only after identity proofing in accordance with clause 4.3, at the same assurance level as required for initial issuance, has been completed for that person.

## Guidelines

- A person who has lost their phone number or e-mail address changes their contact details by proving who they are again.
- Without an alternative route, a person who lost a contact method would be locked out of every future issuance; with a weaker route, an attacker would use it to take over the contact methods.
- The route uses the same identity proofing as the initial issuance, and the notice of ISS-5.7-23 still applies to the previous contact methods.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the replacement route and by examining records of such replacements for the identity proofing event.

ISS-5.7-25: The PID Provider shall flag, for investigation, a network origin indicator recorded under ISS-5.7-13 that is linked to issuance or renewal requests for more than a defined number of distinct national identification numbers within a defined period.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider flags a network origin from which requests for many different persons arrive in a short period.
- A fraudster who operates a farm of devices or an anonymising network to open Wallet Units in the name of many victims is not visible from any single request, but is visible when requests for many identities share the same origin.
- The number and the period are determined as part of the risk assessment. Flagged cases follow the procedure of ISS-5.7-15. The PID Provider sees the network origin only for its own issuances; it does not receive a device identifier, consistent with ISS5.3-02.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the detection rules and their configuration and by examining records of past flags and of the investigations that followed.

ISS-5.7-26: The PID Provider shall limit the retention of the network origin indicators recorded under ISS-5.7-13 to a period determined as part of its risk assessment.

## Guidelines

- Network origin data are kept only as long as the fraud detection needs them.
- Long-lived records of network origin build up a profile of where people are, long after the fraud detection has any use for it.
- Deletion of expired records is automatic. The retention period is long enough for the period used in ISS-5.7-25.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the risk assessment and the retention configuration, and by examining that records older than the retention period are absent.

ISS-5.7-27: The PID Provider shall use the network origin indicators recorded under ISS5.7-13 for no purpose other than the detection of fraud.

## Guidelines

- Network origin data serve fraud detection and nothing else.
- Data collected as a fraud control that are reused for other purposes, such as profiling or analytics, would turn the control into surveillance.
- Access to the records is limited to the staff and systems that operate the detection and investigation under ISS-5.7-15.
- A CAB verifies this requirement by reviewing the access rules and the documented purposes of the records, and by examining access logs.

## 6 Lifecycle Event: PID Batch Replenishment {#s-6}

Purpose of this chapter: Govern the silent, autonomous replenishment of a Wallet Unit's supply of once-only Technical PIDs. When the number of unused Technical PIDs held by the Wallet Unit falls below a defined threshold, additional Technical PIDs are re-issued to the Wallet Unit without any user action and without renewed identity proofing, so that the Wallet User can continue to present a PID without interruption. This chapter covers the technical requirements that govern the batch replenishment interaction between the PID Provider and the Wallet Unit. NOTE: Batch replenishment does not re-verify the identity of the Wallet User; it relies on the identity proofing performed at the most recent initial issuance or renewal. Where renewed identity proofing is required (for example on expiry of the PID validity period), the PID Renewal event applies instead.

### 6.1 Replenishment Triggers and Threshold {#s-6-1}

REP-6.1-01: ISS-4.4-01 applies in this context as well.

REP-6.1-02: The PID Provider shall not replenish Technical PIDs to a Wallet Unit for which the Administrative Validity Period has ended.

## Guidelines

- Once the Administrative Validity Period has ended, the silent replenishment path is closed for that Wallet Unit, and obtaining a new PID afterwards requires a fresh issuance or renewal process that includes identity proofing.
- This prevents replenishment from being used to silently re-supply a person whose PID was revoked by a competent authority for fraud or loss of eligibility, bypassing the identity proofing at Assurance Level High that re-establishment demands.
- The revocation state is read from the PID Provider's own administration and status service, in which every Logical PID's status is maintained.
- A CAB verifies that a replenishment request referencing a revoked Logical PID is refused, by inspecting the status-service linkage and testing the flow against a revoked Logical PID.

REP-6.1-03: The PID Provider shall verify, before issuing replenished Technical PIDs, that the attribute values of the Logical PID remain current.

## Guidelines

- Before replenishing, the PID Provider confirms that the Logical PID does not need to change, that is, that the attribute values it would place into the new Technical PIDs still match the authoritative record.
- Without this check, silent replenishment keeps creating Technical PIDs that carry attribute values which have since changed at the authoritative source, so the person continues to present out-of-date data long after the underlying facts changed.
- Currency can be confirmed by re-reading the authoritative population register, or by acting on a change notification from it.
- A CAB reviews how the PID Provider establishes attribute currency at replenishment and verifies that replenishment does not proceed with stale values when the source record has changed.

REP-6.1-04: The PID Provider shall revoke the outstanding Technical PIDs of a Logical PID when a revocation condition for that Logical PID is established.

## Guidelines

- A revocation condition for a Logical PID arises for cause, for example loss of eligibility, a security incident, or at the person's request. When such a condition is applicable, then it is applicable to all technical PIDs that are issued for that logical which means they all need to be revoked.
- Without this control, revoking a Logical PID would leave batch-issued copies of it valid and presentable, so a person or a Relying Party could continue to rely on a credential the PID Provider itself has already invalidated.
- Revocation is effected through the status service in which each Technical PID is registered under its Logical PID, while the detailed revocation procedure is governed by the PID lifecycle events specification.
- A CAB verifies that a revocation condition for a Logical PID results in every registered still valid Technical PID of it being set to revoked in the status service, for instance by testing the scenario against a Technical PID that has not yet reached the end of its own validity period.

REP-6.1-05: The PID Provider shall not continue automatic replenishment to a Wallet Unit for which it has received an indication that the Wallet Unit or its device is no longer under the legitimate user's control.

## Guidelines

- On any reliable signal that the Wallet Unit or its device has been lost, stolen, or otherwise placed outside the legitimate user's control, the PID Provider stops the silent replenishment stream to that Wallet Unit.
- Without this control, a valid but misappropriated refresh token keeps yielding fresh batches to an attacker's device or a duplicate device indefinitely, because the victim's own wallet keeps working and nothing else signals a problem.
- Qualifying indications include revocation of the Wallet Instance Attestation, a reported loss or theft, or a fraud flag raised on the Logical PID, and the PID Provider treats continued replenishment as conditional on the absence of such an indication.
- A CAB verifies that replenishment stops after a loss, theft, or Wallet Unit revocation indication is recorded, for instance by reviewing which signals halt replenishment and testing the scenario.

REP-6.1-06: The PID Provider shall not treat an indication that a Wallet Unit or its device is no longer under the legitimate user's control as qualifying under REP-5.1-05 unless the reliability of that indication has been established through a defined verification procedure.

## Guidelines

- Before an indication of lost control is allowed to halt replenishment under REP-5.1-05, the PID Provider passes it through a defined procedure that establishes whether the indication is genuine and attributable to a trustworthy source.
- Without this check, an attacker or an unreliable third party could fabricate or relay a false report that a Wallet Unit or its device is no longer under the legitimate user's control, causing the PID Provider to cut the legitimate user off from further Technical PIDs even though nothing is actually wrong.
- A defined verification procedure typically authenticates the reporting channel (for example the Wallet Provider, a government authority, or the user's own authenticated channel) and corroborates the content of the report before it is acted upon; qualifying indications and their expected sources are addressed in REP-5.1-05.

- A CAB verifies that an unauthenticated or uncorroborated report is not sufficient on its own to halt replenishment, for instance by reviewing the verification procedure and testing a fabricated report.

REP-6.1-07: The PID Provider shall record the timestamp and the Technical-PID count of each batch replenishment performed for a Wallet Unit.

## Guidelines

- Each time the PID Provider replenishes a Wallet Unit's batch of Technical PIDs, it records when this happened and how many Technical PIDs were issued.
- Without this record, a Wallet Unit or device no longer under the legitimate user's control that continues to receive replenished batches on a stolen or replayed token would show no trace an investigator could use to notice the abnormal replenishment activity.
- This is typically an addition to the batch-replenishment processing already required, writing the timestamp and count to the PID Provider's administration alongside the existing token-verification outcome.
- A CAB verifies that batch-replenishment timestamp and count are recorded, for instance by reviewing the administration data and testing the scenario.

REP-6.1-08: The PID Provider shall determine, as part of its risk assessment, a maximum batch size and a maximum number of outstanding Technical PIDs per Wallet Unit.

## Guidelines

- As part of its risk assessment, the PID Provider fixes an upper bound on the number of Technical PIDs issued in a single batch and on the number of outstanding Technical PIDs that a Wallet Unit may hold.
- Without a defined upper bound, there is no reference against which an excessive supply of Technical PIDs to a single Wallet Unit could be recognised or contained.
- The bounds follow from the once-only consumption rate over the PID validity period, balancing availability against privacy and abuse resistance, consistent with the reusepolicy parameters of the issuance protocol [5].
- A CAB verifies that the PID Provider has determined a maximum batch size and a maximum outstanding-count per Wallet Unit, for instance by reviewing the risk assessment and the resulting configured limits.

REP-6.1-09: The PID Provider shall not exceed the maximum batch size or the maximum number of outstanding Technical PIDs per Wallet Unit, determined under REP-5.1-08, when replenishing a Wallet Unit.

## Guidelines

- When replenishing a Wallet Unit, the PID Provider stays within the maximum batch size and the maximum outstanding-count determined under REP-5.1-08.
- Enforcing the bounds prevents a compromised or misbehaving Wallet Unit from obtaining an unlimited supply of Technical PIDs, limiting the impact of a successful attack.
- Before issuing, the replenishment process checks the requested batch size and the Wallet Unit's current outstanding count against the determined limits and does not issue Technical PIDs beyond them.
- A CAB verifies that replenishment does not exceed the determined limits, for instance by testing a replenishment request that would exceed the maximum batch size or the maximum outstanding-count.

REP-6.1-10: The PID Provider shall, when it establishes that the attribute values held for a person by the Authentic Source have changed from those carried by the outstanding Technical PIDs of the Logical PID, revoke the outstanding Technical PIDs that carry the superseded values.

## Guidelines

- When the Authentic Source record for a person changes, the PID Provider revokes the Technical PIDs still outstanding that carry the superseded values, so that data the PID Provider no longer attests to can no longer be presented. The corresponding issuance of Technical PIDs carrying the new values is required by REP-5.1-11.
- Without this control, Technical PIDs carrying attribute values the PID Provider no longer attests to would remain valid and presentable, so a Relying Party could receive superseded data.
- The change is detected as part of the currency check of REP-5.1-03, by re-reading the Authentic Source or acting on a change notification from it; the revocation of the superseded Technical PIDs is effected through the status service in which each Technical PID is registered, while the detailed revocation procedure is governed by the PID lifecycle events specification. This replenishment does not repeat identity proofing, which is required only at renewal.
- A CAB verifies that a change in the Authentic Source attribute values results in every outstanding Technical PID carrying the superseded values being set to revoked, for instance by testing the scenario against the status service.

REP-6.1-11: The PID Provider shall, when it establishes that the attribute values held for a person by the Authentic Source have changed from those carried by the outstanding Technical PIDs of the Logical PID, henceforth issue new Technical PIDs carrying the updated attribute values.

## Guidelines

- When the Authentic Source record for a person changes, the PID Provider henceforth issues Technical PIDs carrying the new attribute values to the Wallet Unit, so that current data remains available for presentation. This issuance accompanies the revocation of the superseded Technical PIDs required by REP-5.1-10.
- Without this control, new Technical PIDs could still contain data that is not valid anymore.
- The new Technical PIDs are issued through the batch replenishment path, carrying the attribute values confirmed current under REP-5.1-03; the change is detected as part of that same currency check, by re-reading the Authentic Source or acting on a change notification from it. This issuance does not repeat identity proofing, which is required only at renewal.
- A CAB verifies that a change in the Authentic Source attribute values results in replenished Technical PIDs carrying the new values being issued to the Wallet Unit, for instance by testing the scenario against the status service.

### 6.2 Batch Request and Issuance Protocol {#s-6-2}

REP-6.2-01: ISS-4.6-02 applies also in the context of replenishment.

REP-6.2-02: The PID Provider shall verify the authenticity and integrity of the refresh token presented in a replenishment request.

## Guidelines

- Before acting on a replenishment request, the PID Provider checks that the refresh token was genuinely issued by it and has not been altered.
- Without this check, a forged or tampered token could drive the issuance of Technical PIDs without any valid entitlement behind them.
- Authenticity and integrity are established cryptographically, for example by verifying the PID Provider's own signature or protection over the token.
- A CAB verifies that a token failing authenticity or integrity verification is rejected and that no Technical PID is issued in that case.

REP-6.2-03: The PID Provider shall verify that the refresh token is cryptographically bound to the Wallet Unit that holds the Logical PID to be replenished.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider accepts the token only from the same Wallet Unit and secure cryptographic device that the Logical PID was originally issued to, by requiring a proof of possession that ties the request to a key already bound to that Logical PID.
- Without this binding, a token stolen from the legitimate holder could be used from a different device to obtain genuine Technical PIDs in the victim's name into a wallet the attacker controls.
- A conformant approach requires a proof of possession on the token exchange whose key matches a key bound to an existing Technical PID of the Logical PID, and this is the mechanism that substitutes for the absent identity proofing.
- A CAB verifies that a token presented without the matching device-bound proof of possession is rejected.

REP-6.2-04: The PID Provider shall reject a replenishment request whose refresh token is expired or has been revoked.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider checks the token's validity window and revocation state and declines any request presenting an expired or revoked token.
- Without this check, a token that is no longer valid for use, because it lapsed or was withdrawn after a security event, would still yield fresh Technical PIDs.
- The revocation state of refresh tokens is maintained by the PID Provider alongside the status of the Logical PID they relate to.
- A CAB verifies replenishment with an expired token and with a revoked token and confirms both are refused.

REP-6.2-05: ISS-4.2-04 applies also in the context of replenishment.

REP-6.2-06: The PID Provider shall verify, using the key provenance attestation provided for a batch of replenished Technical PIDs, that the PID binding key pair of every Technical PID in that batch is generated and held in a cryptographic device certified at a level appropriate for Assurance Level High.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider checks the key provenance evidence supplied with a replenishment batch and confirms it covers every Technical PID in that batch, each bound to a key generated and held in a device certified at the level appropriate for Assurance Level High.

- Without this check, a batch could be accepted on provenance evidence that does not actually cover every key in it, so one or more Technical PIDs in the batch could carry a binding key generated or stored outside a certified device without being caught.
- Key provenance is typically established once per certified device or keystore and can cover the multiple keys generated for a single batch in that device; the check applies to the batch as the unit in which the evidence is supplied, while confirming it accounts for every Technical PID issued in it.
- A CAB verifies that a batch containing a Technical PID whose key is not covered by adequate provenance evidence is not issued, for instance by reviewing the provenance-evidence handling and testing the scenario.

REP-6.2-07: ISS-4.5-05 applies also in the context of replenishment.

REP-6.2-08: VOID

REP-6.2-09: The PID Provider shall issue each replenished Technical PID as a credential that is distinct from every other Technical PID of the same Logical PID.

## Guidelines

- Each Technical PID in a batch is a distinct credential, so a Wallet Unit can choose to present a given Technical PID only once and to draw on the next Technical PID for the next presentation.
- Without distinctness, the use of different Technical PIDs would not avoid linkability.
- Distinct binding keys and registration per Technical PID allow single-use downstream.
- A CAB inspects a produced batch to confirm the Technical PIDs are mutually distinct.

REP-6.2-10: The PID Provider shall not release a replenished Technical PID to the Wallet Unit before verification of the refresh token and validation of the Wallet Unit have completed successfully.

## Guidelines

- No Technical PID leaves the PID Provider until the refresh token has been verified and the requesting Wallet Unit has been validated.
- Without this ordering, Technical PID content could be released on the basis of an unverified token or to an unvalidated Wallet Unit, disclosing PID data prematurely.
- At replenishment the release gate rests on the token and Wallet Unit checks, since identity proofing and holder authentication are not repeated.
- A CAB verifies that no Technical PID is released when token verification or Wallet Unit validation has not completed successfully.

REP-6.2-11: The PID Provider shall deliver each replenished Technical PID to the Wallet Unit over a channel that provides confidentiality, integrity, and endpoint authentication bound to the authenticated Wallet Unit.

## Guidelines

- Technical PIDs are delivered only over a channel that keeps them confidential, detects modification, and authenticates the endpoint as the Wallet Unit the replenishment was authorised for.
- Without such a channel, a party interposed on the replenishment exchange could intercept, alter, or redirect the delivered Technical PIDs.
- The channel's endpoint authentication is bound to the same authenticated Wallet Unit whose token and attestation were verified earlier in the flow.
- A CAB verifies that delivery fails when confidentiality, integrity, or endpoint authentication is absent, for instance by inspecting the transport configuration and testing the scenario.

REP-6.2-12: ISS-4.7-01 applies also in the context of replenishment.

REP-6.2-13: ISS-4.7-04 applies also in the context of replenishment.

REP-6.2-14: The PID Provider shall protect any exchange with the authentic source performed during replenishment against interception and modification.

## Guidelines

- Where replenishment involves contacting the authoritative source to confirm that attribute values remain current, that exchange is protected so it cannot be read or altered in transit.
- Without protection, an attacker interposed on the provider-to-source exchange could suppress or alter a change, causing replenishment to proceed with attacker-influenced or stale attribute values.
- Protection provides confidentiality, integrity, and authentication of both endpoints of the exchange with the authentic source.
- A CAB verifies the channel's behaviour when integrity or authentication is absent, for instance by inspecting the provider-to-source channel configuration and testing that behaviour.

### 6.3 Offline Fallback {#s-6-3}

NOTE: A Wallet Unit that anticipates being temporarily unable to reach the PID Provider maintains continuity of use through the stock of once-only Technical PIDs already issued to it, and may manually trigger an out-of-cycle replenishment request before the anticipated period offline. Determining when to trigger such a request, and sizing its stock accordingly, is a Wallet Unit responsibility and is outside the scope of the present document. Where the Wallet Unit does trigger such a request, the requirements of clauses 5.1 and 5.2 apply to it in the same way as to a threshold-triggered request; no separate PID Provider obligation arises from the request being manually triggered.

### 6.4 Exhausted Credential Cleanup {#s-6-4}

REP-6.4-01: The PID Provider shall mark a Technical PID as expired or inactive in its administration once its technical validity period has ended or the Wallet Unit has reported that it was not accepted.

## Guidelines

- Once a Technical PID's technical validity period ends, or the Wallet Unit reports that a replenished Technical PID was not accepted, the PID Provider marks it as inactive in its administration, distinguishing it from the Technical PIDs still current and available for presentation.
- Without this, expired or refused Technical PIDs would remain indistinguishable from current ones in the administration, obscuring which Technical PIDs a Wallet Unit can still present and complicating status and expiry handling. The PID Provider has no general means of detecting that a Technical PID has actually been presented and used, since presentation happens directly between the Wallet Unit and a Relying Party without the PID Provider's involvement, and a Wallet Unit may request a further batch before its existing Technical PIDs are used up; use, as such, is therefore not a trigger for this requirement.

- Marking a Technical PID as inactive changes its administrative state only; it does not remove the record of the Technical PID, its history, or the associated audit log entries, which remain available as required elsewhere in this clause.
- A CAB verifies that a Technical PID whose technical validity period has ended, or that was reported not accepted, is marked as inactive in the administration, for instance by reviewing the administration state against a Technical PID in each condition.

REP-6.4-02: The PID Provider shall retain the audit log entries relating to a Technical PID for the defined retention period, including after that Technical PID has been marked as inactive in the PID Provider's administration.

## Guidelines

- The audit log entries about a Technical PID survive that Technical PID being marked as inactive and remain available for the whole defined retention period.
- Without this, a cleanup or state-management routine that also discarded log data would erase the evidence needed to investigate an incident or demonstrate conformity after a Technical PID is marked as inactive.
- This complements the requirement to create the log entries and the requirement that changes only the administrative state of a Technical PID, not its log history.
- A CAB verifies that log entries for a Technical PID marked as inactive are still present within the retention period, for instance by testing the scenario.

REP-6.4-03: The PID Provider shall determine the retention period referred to in REP-5.4-02 as part of its risk assessment.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider sets the retention period for audit log entries relating to a Technical PID as an outcome of its risk assessment.
- An arbitrary or unbounded retention period would either discard data needed for later investigation or retain personal data longer than justified, conflicting with data minimisation.
- The risk assessment weighs the need for after-the-fact investigation against dataminimisation obligations to fix a defined retention period.
- A CAB verifies that the retention period is defined and traceable to the risk assessment, for instance by reviewing the risk assessment and the configured retention setting.

## 7 Lifecycle Event: PID Renewal {#s-7}

Purpose of this chapter: Enable secure re-issuance of a Logical PID when it is approaching expiry. Renewal is treated as a lifecycle event distinct from initial issuance and always requires renewed identity proofing of the user.

### 7.1 Renewal Triggers and Conditions {#s-7-1}

REN-7.1-01: The PID Provider shall not perform Batch Replenishment of a Logical PID after its Administrative Validity Period has ended without Renewal.

## Guidelines

- Batch Replenishment supplies Technical PIDs only within a current Administrative Validity Period; it cannot bridge the end of that period. Once the Administrative Validity Period has ended, the only way to obtain further Technical PIDs of the Logical PID is a Renewal, which repeats identity proofing and establishes a new Administrative Validity Period.
- Without this rule, Batch Replenishment, which does not repeat identity proofing, could keep supplying Technical PIDs indefinitely beyond the period the original identity proofing was intended to cover, so a Wallet Unit that had passed out of the legitimate user's control could continue to receive fresh PIDs without any renewed check.
- So that issuance is not interrupted, the PID Provider initiates the Renewal as the Administrative Validity Period approaches its end; the threshold for treating it as approaching its end is fixed in the PID Provider's documented issuance procedures. This complements REP-5.1-02, which states the same prohibition on the replenishment side.
- A CAB verifies that Batch Replenishment of a Logical PID whose Administrative Validity Period has ended is refused, and that further Technical PIDs are issued only after a Renewal with renewed identity proofing, for instance by testing a replenishment request submitted after the end of the Administrative Validity Period and confirming it is refused.
- REN-7.1-02: REP-5.1-02 applies also in the context of renewal.
- REN-7.1-03: ISS-4.1-02 applies also in the context of renewal.
- REN-7.1-04: ISS-4.1-03 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.1-05: The PID Provider shall record the timestamp of each renewal request together with the outcome of the re-identification performed for that request.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider keeps a timestamped record of every renewal request and whether the re-identification performed for it succeeded or failed.
- Without a timestamped record of renewal attempts and their re-identification outcome, a pattern such as repeated renewals shortly after each other, or a renewal immediately following a failed or borderline re-identification, would leave no trace for the PID Provider to later notice.
- This extends the renewal logging already required for tamper-evidence with the specific fields needed for pattern analysis: timestamp and re-identification outcome.
- A CAB verifies that renewal records include timestamp and re-identification outcome, for instance by reviewing the renewal log and testing the scenario.

REN-7.1-06: The PID Provider shall flag, for investigation, a Logical PID whose renewal requests show a frequency or a pattern relative to re-identification outcomes that exceeds a defined threshold.

## Guidelines

- When renewal requests for a Logical PID occur more frequently than a defined threshold, or show a pattern such as repeated attempts shortly after a failed reidentification, the PID Provider raises that Logical PID for investigation.
- A compromised credential or a re-identification step that can be gamed by repeated attempts would otherwise continue to be exploited through renewal indefinitely, because each individual renewal may pass its own checks even though the pattern across renewals is abnormal.
- The threshold and pattern definition are set by the PID Provider's own fraudmanagement process, informed by the records kept under REN-6.1-05.
- A CAB verifies that a renewal pattern exceeding the defined threshold results in the Logical PID being flagged, for instance by reviewing the threshold configuration and testing the scenario.

### 7.2 Re-identification Requirements {#s-7-2}

REN-7.2-01: The PID Provider shall verify the identity of the person to whom the Logical PID was issued, applying the identity-proofing requirements of clause 4.3 at the same assurance level required for initial issuance, before renewing that Logical PID.

## Guidelines

- Renewal repeats, in full, an identity verification with a similar strength as for initial issuance; it does not rely on the identity established at a previous issuance or renewal, whichever ground triggered the current renewal.
- Without a fresh identity verification, a Wallet Unit no longer under the control of the person it was issued to, for example following theft, loss, or an unnoticed duplicate activation, could obtain a further, full-validity PID without passing the checks a new issuance would require.
- The identity verification performed for renewal uses a process and evidentiary requirements with the same strength as for initial issuance, applied at the time of the renewal request; it is not satisfied by referring back to records of an earlier verification.
- A CAB verifies that a renewal is preceded by a complete, fresh identity verification meeting the initial-issuance requirements, for instance by reviewing renewal-flow records and testing the renewal path against an incomplete or missing identity check.

### 7.3 Renewal Request and Authorisation {#s-7-3}

REN-7.3-01: ISS-4.4-01 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.3-02: The PID Provider shall not authorise a renewal unless the person's identity has been verified, no ground precluding renewal is present, and the request has been shown to originate from the Wallet Unit holding the Logical PID to be renewed.

## Guidelines

- The authorisation decision for a renewal is reached only once every one of its required pre-conditions has independently completed successfully.

- Without requiring every precondition, a flaw in server-side state handling could let a renewal reach authorisation despite an incomplete identity verification, an unresolved ground for refusal, or a request that did not actually originate from the legitimate Wallet Unit.
- Implementations commonly enforce this through explicit state tracking of each precondition, only permitting the authorisation step once all recorded states show completion.
- A CAB verifies that authorisation is refused when any one precondition has not completed, for instance by reviewing the authorisation logic and testing each precondition individually.

REN-7.3-03: The PID Provider shall verify that a renewal request is bound to the Logical PID to be renewed by requiring proof of possession of the private key corresponding to the existing PID binding public key of that Logical PID.

## Guidelines

- The renewal request is shown to come from the same Wallet Unit that holds the Logical PID's existing binding key, through a proof-of-possession exchange, before the PID Provider proceeds with re-identification and renewal.
- Without this binding, an attacker holding a duplicate or separately-activated Wallet Unit in the victim's name could request renewal of the victim's Logical PID from a device the victim never controlled.
- A conformant implementation requires a proof of possession on the renewal request whose key matches the existing PID binding key of the Logical PID cited in the request.
- A CAB verifies that a renewal request lacking valid proof of possession of the existing binding key is refused, for instance by testing the scenario.

### 7.4 PID Generation and Signing {#s-7-4}

REN-7.4-01: ISS-4.5-01 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.4-02: REP-5.2-14 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.4-03: ISS-4.5-02 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.4-04: ISS-4.5-03 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.4-05: ISS-4.5-04 applies also in the context of renewal.

- REN-7.4-06: ISS-4.2-05 applies also in the context of renewal.
- REN-7.4-07: ISS-4.5-05 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.4-08: ISS-4.5-06 applies also in the context of renewal.

- REN-7.4-09: ISS-4.5-07 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.4-10: ISS-4.5-08 applies also in the context of renewal.

### 7.5 Delivery of the PID {#s-7-5}

REN-7.5-01: ISS-4.6-01 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.5-02: ISS-4.6-02 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.5-03: ISS-4.6-04 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.5-04: ISS-4.6-05 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.5-05: ISS-4.7-01 applies also in the context of renewal.

REN-7.5-06: The PID Provider shall notify the identified person, over a channel that ensures the integrity and authenticity of the notification and is independent of the Wallet Unit, when their Logical PID has been renewed.

## Guidelines

- The PID Provider sends the person a notification, delivered independently of the Wallet Unit and protected against undetected alteration or spoofing, each time their Logical PID is renewed.
- Without an integrity- and authenticity-protected channel, a renewal notification could be suppressed or spoofed, so a person would not learn that their PID was renewed, for example following an unauthorised renewal from a duplicate Wallet Unit.
- This uses the same class of out-of-band channel, protected in the same way, as other notifications the PID Provider sends independently of the Wallet Unit.
- A CAB verifies that a renewal triggers the notification and that the channel used protects its integrity and authenticity, for instance by reviewing the notification mechanism and testing the scenario.

REN-7.5-07: ISS-4.7-04 applies also in the context of renewal.

## Annex A (informative): PID State Diagram {#s-a}

NOTE: This annex is informative and does not contain normative requirements.

The lifecycle events after issuance - PID revocation, expiry and deletion - are specified in the PID Lifecycle Events specification [7].

## Overview

This annex proposes an updated Technical PID state model, built on the NOID/ARF baseline state model and revised for ARF v3.0.0 and for the lifecycle events foreseen in this specification (Initial Issuance, Batch Replenishment, and Renewal - LE-01, LE-02, and LE03). Each state (Created, Issued, Valid, Expired, Revoked, Cancelled) applies to an individual Technical PID, and a seventh, Wallet-side state (Deleted) accounts for user-initiated deletion in the wallet. A Logical PID is only the type of PID and has no state of its own; whether the PID Provider may issue further Technical PIDs to a Wallet Unit without renewed identity proofing is governed by the Administrative Validity Period, not by any state of the Logical PID.

The diagram below is illustrative; the normative rules governing each transition are stated in the requirements of Chapters 4, 5, and 6 of this specification, referenced alongside each transition.

![Image](/img/edi-stelsel/2026-11-06/nl-p-04p-part-1/image_000000_1fb389e73b4ce066e6b731afabc1b5d54524f15305b930f0ed440029c2c252eb.png)

## Definitions: Renewal, Batch Replenishment, Re-issuance, and Initial Issuance

Batch Replenishment: Batch Replenishment (LE-02) supplies further Technical PIDs of an existing Logical PID without renewed identity proofing, subject to the once-only-token and loss-of-control controls of Chapter 5. It also covers re-issuance with updated attribute values when these change at the Authentic Source, in which case the Technical PIDs carrying the superseded values are revoked (REP-5.1-10).

Renewal: Renewal (LE-03) always repeats identity verification at the assurance level required for initial issuance, and is triggered by the Administrative Validity Period approaching its end (REN-6.1-01). A change in the attribute values held by the Authentic Source is handled as Batch Replenishment (LE-02), not as a renewal, in line with the ARF.

Initial Issuance: Initial Issuance (LE-01) is the first PID issued to a Wallet Unit for a person or an issuance where a previous Logical PID for the same person exists but its Administrative Validity Period has ended and its Technical PIDs have been revoked. A fresh initial issuance - with full identity proofing - is then the only route back in.

| Circumstance                                                                                   | Classification                                     | Why                      |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
| No previous Logical PID for the person                                                         | Initial Issuance (LE-01)                           | ISS-4.1-01               |
| Existing Logical PID, unchanged attributes, more Technical PIDs needed                         | Batch Replenishment (LE-02)                        | REP-5.1-01 .. REP-5.1-08 |
| Existing Logical PID, Administrative Validity Period approaching its end, no attribute change  | Renewal (LE-03)                                    | REN-6.1-01               |
| Existing Logical PID, attribute values changed at the Authentic Source                         | Batch Replenishment (LE-02)                        | REP-5.1-03, REP-5.1-10   |
| Existing Logical PID, Administrative Validity Period ended and previous Technical PIDs revoked | Initial Issuance (LE-01) only                      | REN-6.1-02, REP-5.1-02   |
| Wallet Unit reports the PID as not accepted after delivery                                     | Revocation of that PID (not a new lifecycle event) | ISS-4.6-05, REN-6.5-04   |
| User deletes the PID in the wallet                                                             | Wallet-side Deletion (LE-06)                       |                          |

## States

| State   | Origin                        | Terminal?   | Meaning                                                                                                                      |
|---------|-------------------------------|-------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Created | PID Provider-internal (NOID) | No          | PID generated at the Provider, before delivery to the Wallet Unit.                                                           |
| Issued  | ARF-defined                   | No          | PID has left the Provider's systems and been delivered to the Wallet Unit.                                                   |
| Valid   | ARF-defined                   | No          | Validity start date reached; the PID is usable. Batch Replenishment and Renewal keep the Logical PID in this state.          |
| Expired | ARF-defined                   | Yes         | Validity period has ended.                                                                                                   |
| Revoked | ARF-defined                   | Yes         | Permanently invalidated, whether Provider-initiated, User-initiated, or following a not-accepted report for a delivered PID. |
| Cancelled              | PID Provider-internal (NOID)     | Yes         | Withdrawn before delivery (from Created only). |
| Deleted (Wallet-side) | Wallet-side, not a Provider state | No          | User-initiated deletion in the wallet (LE-06). |

## Transitions Driven by Each Lifecycle Event

LE-01 (Initial Issuance) drives Created → Issued → Valid, or Created → Cancelled if withdrawn before delivery.

LE-02 (Batch Replenishment) adds further Technical PIDs within the Administrative Validity Period of an existing, Logical PID; the new Technical PIDs pass through Created → Issued → Valid like any others, and no state of the Logical PID changes because a Logical PID has no state of its own. Where the replenishment reflects changed attribute values, the Technical PIDs carrying the superseded values are additionally driven to Revoked (REP-5.1-10).

LE-03 (Renewal) issues further Technical PIDs after renewed identity proofing and opens a new Administrative Validity Period.

Delivered-PID withdrawal, at any point after Issued, drives that PID to Revoked, never to Cancelled (ISS-4.7-03).

A not-accepted report for a PID already classified as issued drives it to Revoked (ISS-4.6-05, REN-6.5-04).

User-initiated deletion in the wallet drives the Wallet Unit's copy to Deleted (Wallet-side). Since there is not notification to the PID Provider of this event, this is not leading to a change in state at the PID Provider side.
